+Duties stack. For a given part, add the layers that apply:
+1. Base HTS rate (often 0-4% for electronics and motors).
+2. Section 301 China, technology-transfer lists: 25% (Lists 1-3) or 7.5% (List 4A). Four-year
+   review raised strategic lines: semiconductors 50% (from Jan 1, 2025), non-EV lithium-ion
+   batteries 25% and permanent magnets 25% (both from Jan 1, 2026).
+3. Section 301 forced-labor action (since July 24, 2026): +12.5% on China and most economies,
+   +10% on 17 (incl. Canada, Mexico, UK, India). USMCA-qualifying goods and Section 232 goods
+   are exempt. This replaced the Section 122 10% surcharge, which replaced the IEEPA tariffs
+   the Supreme Court struck down on Feb 20, 2026.
+   Example: Chinese-origin MCU pays 50% Section 301; a Malaysian-origin one pays 0.
+4. Section 232 metals (rebuilt Apr 6, 2026, on full customs value): steel/aluminum/most copper
+   articles 50%; listed derivatives 25%, or 15% for some partners; 10% if the metal is >= 85%
+   US melted/smelted; 0% if under 15% metal by weight outside Ch. 72-76. Hits frames,
+   extrusions, fasteners, wire and cable (copper cable must report smelt/cast country).
+5. Section 232 machinery: handling robots (8428.70) and machining centers pay 15% total through
+   Dec 31, 2027, then the 25% derivative rate. Robots under 8479.50 pay none today.
+6. Section 232 semiconductors (Jan 15, 2026): 25%, but only for narrow AI-accelerator
+   performance bands, and civil industrial/robotics use and startups are exempt. Rarely bites.
+7. Section 232 drones (Sept 3, 2026): only drone aircraft, docks and 8807 drone parts; motors,
+   batteries and cameras under their own codes are not listed. Watch if you share parts with
+8. De minimis: the $800 duty-free exemption is suspended, so small prototype orders from
+9. Upside: IEEPA duties paid in 2025-26 are refundable through CBP's CAPE process
+   ($137.9B in claims by Oct 23, 2026). Worth checking your past entries.
+## C. Supply security (can we keep getting it?)
+1. Rare earths. China Announcement 18 (Apr 2025) still requires a per-order export licence for
+   NdFeB magnets containing terbium or dysprosium (the high-temperature SH/UH/EH grades); MOFCOM
+   has 45 working days and can refuse. The broader Oct 2025 package (incl. a rule reaching
+   foreign-made products containing Chinese rare earths) is suspended only until Jan 10, 2027.
+   MOFCOM has said finished rotors/stators with fixed magnets generally fall outside
+   Announcement 18, so buying a finished motor is less exposed than buying magnets.
+   China's 2024 ban on gallium/germanium/antimony exports to the US is suspended only to
+2. Forced labor (UFLPA). Goods with any Xinjiang input or from Entity List companies (190 as
+   of Oct 29, 2026) are presumed barred; the importer must rebut with "clear and convincing"
+   evidence. High-priority sectors include lithium, aluminum, copper, steel, PVC, polysilicon:
+   batteries, frames, motors and cable. FY2025: ~7,325 shipments stopped, ~6.5% released.
+3. Entity and military lists. DoD 1260H list (June 2026) added Unitree, Hesai, RoboSense, CALB,
+   EVE Energy, BOE, TP-Link and others; mainly a defense-customer and reputational risk. BIS
+   "Affiliates Rule" (50%-owned subsidiaries of listed entities) is suspended to Jan 10, 2027.
+4. Domestic capacity is thin for reducers, frameless motors, magnets and lidar; expect
+   qualification backlogs and price premiums (Sustainment, Sept 2026).
+- Jan 10, 2027: China rare-earth suspension and BIS Affiliates Rule suspension both lapse
+- Apr 26, 2027: Section 232 robotics/industrial machinery negotiation update due (Proclamation
+  11077, Oct 28, 2026, found a national-security threat but imposed no tariff yet).
+- May 24 / Jun 23, 2027: Section 301 Chinese legacy-chip tariff rises from 0% to a rate to be
+- Jan 1, 2029: 75% threshold; firmware-update waiver runs at least to here.
+- Canada-US: USMCA not renewed on Jul 1, 2026 (stays in force, annual reviews); Canada broke
+  off talks Aug 22, counter-tariffs on ~C$27.6B of US goods (incl. electronics) since Sep 8;
+  US Section 338 duties and import bans on some Canadian vehicles, dairy, alcohol. A Canadian
+  company importing US parts into Canada may pay Canadian counter-tariffs.
+## E. Ordinary commercial factors (still decide most purchases)
+Unit price and price breaks, MOQ, lead time and stock depth, freight and brokerage, FX
+(CAD/USD), payment terms, NRE/tooling for custom parts, qualification and first-article time,
+second source availability, lifecycle/EOL risk, authorized channel vs broker (counterfeits),
+warranty/support, shipping certifications (UN38.3 for batteries), and now: whether the
+1. Sentinel Automata, "Will your robot pass the FCC's 65% test?" - clearest worked example.
+2. Sidley, FCC robotics listing analysis - authoritative legal framing.
+3. HTSBase, Section 301 China tariffs in 2026 - the tariff stack in one page.
+4. Mainrich, which magnets need a Chinese export licence (Nov 2026).
+5. Sustainment, "A new standard for building American in robotics" - practical sourcing view.
+- FCC FAQ robots/inverters (quoted by several sources, not yet opened by us):
+- Gatewell, how a product qualifies (component cost rules):
+- Gatewell Protocol for Origin Evidence v1.0 (evidence file + BOM schema):
+- Lotus International, subassembly strategy and FCC 26-50:
+- ABA, IEEPA struck down and Section 122 expired:
+- GingerControl, Section 232 robotics proclamation and what machinery pays now:
+- Findchips, semiconductor tariffs for BOM pricing: https://blog.findchips.com/semiconductor-tariffs-2026/
+- YC RFS, Robots Made in America: https://www.ycombinator.com/rfs#robots-made-in-america
+# 03 Review of handoff v2 (Sat Nov 21, 2026, 3pm EST)
+Verdict: GO. v2 is a stronger pitch than v1 and the riskiest piece (CAD regeneration) works.
+Six things in the checks and the agent schema are wrong or will break on real motors; fix them
+before anyone writes the check code. Schedule has already slipped one milestone.
+- CadQuery 2.8.0 installs from pip on Python 3.12 (local spike, not committed; superseded by `cad/cad_worker/` on main). A parametric robot
+  (base, e-box, 2 wheels, 2 motors, 2 brackets, caster) regenerates for NEMA 17/23/34 and exports
+  GLB + STEP in about 0.25 s per variant. GLB keeps part names (`bracket_L`, `motor_R`, ...), so
+  the viewer can highlight the bracket by name. Spike placement has bugs (one motor sits on the
+  wrong side); the toolchain is fine. Pin Python 3.12 in the Docker image (3.13 untested).
+- Legal claim in v2 section 3 checked against 48 CFR 25.003 (eCFR, current to Nov 19, 2026):
+  a domestic end product needs "components mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States"
+  above 65%. A US-made motor counts whole, whatever its magnets. Confirmed.
+  - Correction: the iron/steel exception is about END PRODUCTS that are >50% iron/steel by cost,
+    not about components. A robot is not, so drop "(except iron and steel)".
+  - New, flag for counsel, do not build: the same text says foreign components "of the same
+    class or kind" the government has found not available domestically (FAR 25.104 list) are
+    treated as domestic. Whether the FCC applies that is unknown.
+- Real US-made NEMA targets found (evidence tier in brackets):
+  - Teknic ClearPath-SD (integrated servo, NEMA 23/34, from $265; NEMA 17 "available later this
+    year"). Site: "we'll build and ship it to you from our New York manufacturing plant". [T2]
+  - Moog Animatics SmartMotor SM23165D and others: news page says "produced in our Murphy, NC
+    facility" and names SKUs. [T1-ish: model-specific statement]
+  - Pittman (AMETEK), NEMA 23 brushless: only an HQ address in Harleysville, PA. [T3, not
+    evidence] A good live example of the verifier refusing a weak claim.
+  - Every credible US-made candidate found is a servo/BLDC, not a stepper. That matters below.
+1. The schema makes the LLM do arithmetic. `rated_torque_nm`, `body_length_mm`, `price_usd`
+   force the agent to convert oz-in, lb-in, inches, CAD. That breaks the "LLM never does math"
+   rule and breaks the verbatim verifier (the page says "425 oz-in", not "3.0"). Fix: capture
+   value + unit exactly as written (`torque: {value: 425, unit: "oz-in", quote: "..."}`); code
+2. Steppers break torque, speed and voltage checks.
+   - Stepper "torque" on a page is holding torque; usable torque falls with speed.
+   - Stepper "rated voltage" is winding voltage (2-4 V), so every stepper fails V_bus.
+   Fix: add `motor_type` (servo | bldc | stepper | brushed). Servo/BLDC: continuous torque,
+   rated speed, supply voltage range. Stepper: torque at operating speed from the pull-out curve
+   if the datasheet has one, else Review with a stated derate. Pick a demo baseline and
+   candidates that are servos/BLDC; that is also what the US makers sell.
+3. Gear ratio is unstated. Computed with the v2 formula (r = 60 mm, 2 motors, G = 1, eta 0.9,
+   Crr 0.02, a = 0.5 m/s^2, SF 1.5): 5 kg flat = 0.174 Nm per motor; 5 kg on 5 deg = 0.388 Nm;
+   15 kg on 10 deg = 1.80 Nm. Wheel speed at 1 m/s = 159 rpm. A light (~5 kg) indoor robot
+   works direct-drive with NEMA 23 servos; a heavier one needs a gearbox, which is another part
+   with its own origin and flange. Recommendation: ~5 kg, direct drive, G = 1 fixed.
+4. Fit check misses the constraint that actually bites: motor axis sits at wheel-axle height,
+   so the flange hangs below it. Ground clearance = r - frame/2 - clearance - plate. In the spike
+   NEMA 34 on 60 mm wheels leaves about 4 mm. Add it. Also add bolt hole size to the NEMA table
+   (NEMA 17 M3; NEMA 23 ~5.1 mm through; NEMA 34 ~5.5 mm through, verify per vendor drawing).
+5. Datasheet numbers cannot be string-matched against page HTML. Verify PDF-derived values
+   against the PDF text layer (pdftotext). Values Gemini read from an image or a curve are
+   "unverified": they can make a candidate Review, never Pass*.
+6. "38% -> 67%" must come out of a real BOM, not the script. Replacing two drive motors moves
+   ~29 points only if they are a large share of component cost. Build the BOM first and let
+   the calculator pick the line; remember duty and freight count in foreign parts' cost.
+- Now ~3pm EST Sat. The "Sat 2pm: bracket regenerates" milestone has passed unless a teammate
+  hit it; the spike covers most of it. ~13 h to the 4am freeze.
+- v2 touches 9 sponsor technologies (TinyFish x5 products, Gemini, Vultr, Tiger Data, Auth0,
+  - Must: TinySearch/TinyFetch + TinyAgent with live tiles, Fetch-HTML verifier, Gemini
+  - Should: Vultr deploy, Tiger Data agent_runs + success-by-site panel (doubles as TinyFish
+  - Could: TinyBrowser RFQ form, TinyMonitor, tournament of 3, Auth0, GoDaddy, Entire extras.
+- Ask organizers whether a team can win more than one MLH prize (unverified).
+"What if the motor is not NEMA?" Answer: the engine regenerates parts defined by a mechanical
+interface standard (NEMA flanges today; ISO 9409 tool flanges, DIN rail, standard bearing
+sizes next). Say "parametric template" on stage, as v2 already plans.

1	# Hack Western 13 handoff v3: build package (AI Robot Redesign Engine)
2	
3	Written Sat Nov 21, 2026, ~5:15pm EST. Devpost deadline Sun Nov 22, 9am EST. Feature freeze 4am.
4	Build starts in the next session. This file wins over HANDOFF.md (v1) and HANDOFF-v2.md where
5	they disagree; v2 still holds the pitch, demo script and sponsor rules.
6	
7	## 0. Read first (in this order)
8	
9	| File | What | Who |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| `docs/design/architecture.html` | the diagram (open in a browser) | everyone |
12	| `docs/design/07-agent-architecture.md` | agent topology, blackboard SQL, Decision 1, synthesis + advocate contract | Tygo |
13	| `docs/design/04-architecture.md` | pipeline stages, data shapes, fleet scheduler, record/replay, events | Tygo, frontend |
14	| `docs/design/05-checks-spec.md` | units, torque/speed/voltage/fit rules, verdicts, evidence rules | checks owner |
15	| `docs/design/03-v2-review.md` | why the v2 schema/checks changed; real US motor targets | everyone |
16	| `docs/design/02-sourcing-factors.md` | tariffs, FCC test, rare earths, UFLPA, dates | Tygo, data owner |
17	| `docs/design/06-reading-tygo.md` | reading list for the coordination layer | Tygo |
18	| `docs/design/schemas/*.json` | TinyAgent output schema, advocate output schema | builders |
19	| `spikes/check_tf_schema.py` | checks an output_schema against TinyFish rules | Tygo |
20	
21	## 1. The system in one paragraph
22	
23	Code owns the control flow. An orchestrator fans out one worker per BOM line: a swap worker
24	hunts US-made NEMA replacements for the drive motor, and 2-3 origin workers try to prove where
25	current high-cost parts are made. Workers use free TinySearch/TinyFetch for discovery and
26	triage, and TinyAgent (live tiles) only where a page needs clicking. Raw claims go to a code
27	Verifier that re-fetches the page and matches quote and number; only it writes facts to a Tiger
28	Data blackboard that all workers read between runs. Deterministic code computes landed cost,
29	domestic %, risk flags and the engineering checks, ranks three designs, and CadQuery rebuilds the
30	motor bracket. Synthesis: a code case builder, three tightly scoped advocate calls, one writer,
31	and a Gemini Decision 1 critic that can send at most one round of gap requests back to the
32	orchestrator. No LLM produces a number, a verdict or an origin tier.
33	
34	```mermaid
35	flowchart TB
36	  UI["Web app: viewer, live tiles, compliance card"] <-->|SSE| API["FastAPI on Vultr"]
37	  API --> ORCH["Orchestrator: plan, fan out, verify, check, rank, synthesize, build"]
38	  ORCH --> SCH["Fleet scheduler + per-domain circuit breaker"]
39	  SCH --> W1["Swap worker: drive motor"]
40	  SCH --> W2["Origin workers: battery, compute, lidar"]
41	  W1 <--> TF["TinySearch / TinyFetch / TinyAgent / TinyBrowser"]
42	  W2 <--> TF
43	  W1 -->|raw claims| VER["Verifier gate"]
44	  W2 -->|raw claims| VER
45	  VER -->|facts only| BB[("Tiger Data: board, tasks, agent_runs, supplier_obs")]
46	  BB <-->|read board, lease tasks| W1
47	  BB <-->|read board, lease tasks| W2
48	  BB --> DET["Supply-chain math + engineering checks + ranking"]
49	  DET --> CB["Case builder (code)"]
50	  CB --> ADV["3 advocates: cost / performance / US-first"]
51	  ADV --> SYN["Synthesizer"]
52	  SYN --> CRIT["Critic: Gemini Decision 1"]
53	  CRIT -->|gap requests, max 1 round| ORCH
54	  CRIT --> REP["Final report + RFQ draft"]
55	  DET --> CAD["CadQuery bracket, GLB + STEP"]
56	```
57	
58	## 2. Locked decisions (all approved by Tygo)
59	
60	1. Code-owned state machine; LLMs are functions. Workers are code loops, not LLM agents.
61	2. TRIAGE splits extraction: Fetch + Gemini for readable pages, TinyAgent only for interaction.
62	3. Verification: fresh TinyFetch html (`ttl=0`) + PDF text; agent html capture kept as provenance.
63	4. Units table in code (no `pint`); the agent returns value + unit as written.
64	5. Steppers allowed but capped at Review without verified torque at speed.
65	6. SSE to the UI; one FastAPI process, asyncio for I/O, process pool for CadQuery.
66	7. Record/replay client wraps every TinyFish and Gemini call from hour one (LIVE/REPLAY badge).
67	8. Origin tier decided by code rules; Decision 1 can only lower it.
68	9. Blackboard = `board` hypertable + `tasks` table; only the Verifier writes `kind='fact'`.
69	10. Site status lives only in `agent_runs`; orchestrator keeps an in-memory circuit breaker;
70	    `site_success_1h` continuous aggregate is a UI panel only.
71	11. Synthesis = case builder (code) + 3 scoped advocates (2 rounds) + one writer + Decision 1
72	    critic + one gap round. Advocate contract: 07 section 5.
73	12. Gemini Flash for planning, extraction and prose; Gemini Decision 1 for triage routing, run
74	    outcome, origin wording, rubric, gap choice.
75	13. Demo robot: ~5 kg, direct drive (G = 1), 60 mm wheels, NEMA servo baseline. Peak torque
76	    requirement 0.388 N·m per motor at 5 deg, 159 rpm at 1 m/s (computed, 05 section 2).

86	  `run_finished`, `claim_verified`, `claim_rejected`, `check_result`, `compliance`,

88	  Every event: `{type, job_id, ts, data}`. The UI is a pure function of the event log.
89	- SQL: 07 section 3 (`board`, `tasks`, `agent_runs`, `supplier_obs`, `site_success_1h`,

# Hack Western 13 handoff v3: build package (AI Robot Redesign Engine)

Written Sat Nov 21, 2026, ~5:15pm EST. Devpost deadline Sun Nov 22, 9am EST. Feature freeze 4am.
Build starts in the next session. This file wins over HANDOFF.md (v1) and HANDOFF-v2.md where
they disagree; v2 still holds the pitch, demo script and sponsor rules.

## 0. Read first (in this order)

| File | What | Who |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/design/architecture.html` | the diagram (open in a browser) | everyone |
| `docs/design/07-agent-architecture.md` | agent topology, blackboard SQL, Decision 1, synthesis + advocate contract | Tygo |
| `docs/design/04-architecture.md` | pipeline stages, data shapes, fleet scheduler, record/replay, events | Tygo, frontend |
| `docs/design/05-checks-spec.md` | units, torque/speed/voltage/fit rules, verdicts, evidence rules | checks owner |
| `docs/design/03-v2-review.md` | why the v2 schema/checks changed; real US motor targets | everyone |
| `docs/design/02-sourcing-factors.md` | tariffs, FCC test, rare earths, UFLPA, dates | Tygo, data owner |
| `docs/design/06-reading-tygo.md` | reading list for the coordination layer | Tygo |
| `docs/design/schemas/*.json` | TinyAgent output schema, advocate output schema | builders |
| `spikes/check_tf_schema.py` | checks an output_schema against TinyFish rules | Tygo |

## 1. The system in one paragraph

Code owns the control flow. An orchestrator fans out one worker per BOM line: a swap worker
hunts US-made NEMA replacements for the drive motor, and 2-3 origin workers try to prove where
current high-cost parts are made. Workers use free TinySearch/TinyFetch for discovery and
triage, and TinyAgent (live tiles) only where a page needs clicking. Raw claims go to a code
Verifier that re-fetches the page and matches quote and number; only it writes facts to a Tiger
Data blackboard that all workers read between runs. Deterministic code computes landed cost,
domestic %, risk flags and the engineering checks, ranks three designs, and CadQuery rebuilds the
motor bracket. Synthesis: a code case builder, three tightly scoped advocate calls, one writer,
and a Gemini Decision 1 critic that can send at most one round of gap requests back to the
orchestrator. No LLM produces a number, a verdict or an origin tier.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  UI["Web app: viewer, live tiles, compliance card"] <-->|SSE| API["FastAPI on Vultr"]
  API --> ORCH["Orchestrator: plan, fan out, verify, check, rank, synthesize, build"]
  ORCH --> SCH["Fleet scheduler + per-domain circuit breaker"]
  SCH --> W1["Swap worker: drive motor"]
  SCH --> W2["Origin workers: battery, compute, lidar"]
  W1 <--> TF["TinySearch / TinyFetch / TinyAgent / TinyBrowser"]
  W2 <--> TF
  W1 -->|raw claims| VER["Verifier gate"]
  W2 -->|raw claims| VER
  VER -->|facts only| BB[("Tiger Data: board, tasks, agent_runs, supplier_obs")]
  BB <-->|read board, lease tasks| W1
  BB <-->|read board, lease tasks| W2
  BB --> DET["Supply-chain math + engineering checks + ranking"]
  DET --> CB["Case builder (code)"]
  CB --> ADV["3 advocates: cost / performance / US-first"]
  ADV --> SYN["Synthesizer"]
  SYN --> CRIT["Critic: Gemini Decision 1"]
  CRIT -->|gap requests, max 1 round| ORCH
  CRIT --> REP["Final report + RFQ draft"]
  DET --> CAD["CadQuery bracket, GLB + STEP"]
```

## 2. Locked decisions (all approved by Tygo)

1. Code-owned state machine; LLMs are functions. Workers are code loops, not LLM agents.
2. TRIAGE splits extraction: Fetch + Gemini for readable pages, TinyAgent only for interaction.
3. Verification: fresh TinyFetch html (`ttl=0`) + PDF text; agent html capture kept as provenance.
4. Units table in code (no `pint`); the agent returns value + unit as written.
5. Steppers allowed but capped at Review without verified torque at speed.
6. SSE to the UI; one FastAPI process, asyncio for I/O, process pool for CadQuery.
7. Record/replay client wraps every TinyFish and Gemini call from hour one (LIVE/REPLAY badge).
8. Origin tier decided by code rules; Decision 1 can only lower it.
9. Blackboard = `board` hypertable + `tasks` table; only the Verifier writes `kind='fact'`.
10. Site status lives only in `agent_runs`; orchestrator keeps an in-memory circuit breaker;
    `site_success_1h` continuous aggregate is a UI panel only.
11. Synthesis = case builder (code) + 3 scoped advocates (2 rounds) + one writer + Decision 1
    critic + one gap round. Advocate contract: 07 section 5.
12. Gemini Flash for planning, extraction and prose; Gemini Decision 1 for triage routing, run
    outcome, origin wording, rubric, gap choice.
13. Demo robot: ~5 kg, direct drive (G = 1), 60 mm wheels, NEMA servo baseline. Peak torque
    requirement 0.388 N·m per motor at 5 deg, 159 rpm at 1 m/s (computed, 05 section 2).

## 3. Contracts between owners (do not change without telling the others)

- TinyAgent output schema: `docs/design/schemas/motor_candidate.tinyfish.json`
  (passes `spikes/check_tf_schema.py`).
- Advocate output schema: `docs/design/schemas/advocate_output.schema.json`.
- Python data shapes: `Requirement`, `Source`, `Claim`, `OriginEvidence`, `Candidate`,
  `RunRecord` (04 section 4); `CheckResult` (05).
- SSE event types: `stage`, `run_started`, `run_streaming_url`, `run_progress`,
  `run_finished`, `claim_verified`, `claim_rejected`, `check_result`, `compliance`,
  `design_ready`, `advocate`, `synthesis`, `error` (04 section 8, plus the last three).
  Every event: `{type, job_id, ts, data}`. The UI is a pure function of the event log.
- SQL: 07 section 3 (`board`, `tasks`, `agent_runs`, `supplier_obs`, `site_success_1h`,
  `supplier_1h`). Untested; run it on Tiger Cloud first (needs TimescaleDB 2.13+).
- HTTP: `POST /jobs` (BOM + requirement + mode live|replay|mixed), `GET /jobs/{id}`,
  `GET /jobs/{id}/events` (SSE), `GET /designs/{id}/glb`, `GET /designs/{id}/step`.

## 4. Existing code on main vs v3 (teammates already scaffolded from v2)

`main` (PR #1 repo-setup, PR #2 cad-bracket) already has `backend/app/` (FastAPI, `schemas.py`,
`agents/{swarm,datasheet,verifier,rfq}.py` stubs, `engineering/{checks,compliance,nema,tournament}.py`),
`cad/cad_worker/` (parametric robot, NEMA bracket, GLB/STEP; better than `spikes/cad_spike.py`),
`db/schema.sql`, `frontend/` (Vite React), `docker-compose.yml`, `data/demo_robot.json`,
`data/seed_motors.json` (empty), and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` written against v2. Build on it; keep
its module and table names. Deltas to apply in the first build hour:

| Where | Today (v2) | Change to (v3) | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schemas.py` `MotorCandidate` | flat `rated_torque_nm`, `voltage_v`, `price_usd`... | mirror `schemas/motor_candidate.tinyfish.json`: `motor_type`, `specs[] {name, value, unit, at_speed_*, quote, source_url}`, `origin_source_url`; add `Claim`, `Source`, `OriginEvidence` (04 section 4) | 2 + 3 |
| `schemas.py` `RobotRequirements` | `envelope_mm`, one torque requirement | add `min_ground_clearance_mm`, `wheel_bore_mm`, `deck_thickness_mm`; keep `envelope_mm` as inboard room | 3 |
| `schemas.py` `BomRow` | `origin` string | add `origin_tier` (T1/T2/T3/rejected/none), `freight_usd`, `duty_usd`, `hts_code` | 2 + 3 |
| `engineering/checks.py` | single torque check, exact voltage match, no motor type, fit length only | rules in 05: units table, cont + peak torque, per-type speed/voltage, `fit_ground`, `fit_shaft`, real drop_in/close badge | 3 |
| `engineering/compliance.py` | unit cost only; note "COTS treatment: flag for counsel" | landed cost (freight + duty) per FAR 25.003; domestic only if origin tier T1/T2 and US; pass only if strictly > 65%; replace COTS note: FCC FAQ says COTS exception inapplicable (01) | 2 |
| `agents/swarm.py` | one `find_candidates()` | becomes `workers/` swap + origin workers driven by the orchestrator; add `orchestrator/`, `tfclient/` (record/replay), `synth/` (case builder, advocates, synthesizer, critic) under `backend/app/` | 2 |
| `agents/verifier.py` | stub | `classify_outcome`, `verify_claim`, origin tier rules (section 7) | 2 |
| `db/schema.sql` | `agent_runs`, `site_success_hourly`, `price_observations`, `check_results`, `design_variants` | add `board`, `tasks` (07 section 3); `agent_runs` + `job_id`, `product`, `live`, rename `status` -> `outcome` or keep and document; set `site_success_hourly` to `materialized_only = false` and use `sum(CASE ...)` if `FILTER` fails; add `origin_tier` to `price_observations` and a `supplier_1h` cagg on it | 2 |
| `data/seed_motors.json` | empty | Teknic ClearPath-SD NEMA 23, Moog SM23165D, Pittman (T3 example), real fields only | 3 |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | v2 | banner added pointing here; fold v3 in when time allows | 2 |

Names in 07 map to existing ones: `site_success_1h` = `site_success_hourly`,
`supplier_obs` = `price_observations`.

## 5. Owners

| Owner | Area |
|---|---|
| 1 | CAD: robot + bracket in CadQuery (Python 3.12), GLB/STEP, viewer before/after |
| 2 (Tygo) | orchestrator, fleet, tfclient record/replay, workers, verifier, board/tasks, supply math, synthesis loop |
| 3 | checks + units, NEMA table with vendor drawing URLs, demo BOM with real prices and origins, requirement, tariffs.yaml, entity lists |
| 4 | frontend (tiles via iframe of `streaming_url`, compliance card, design tabs with advocate text), Vultr deploy, domain, video, Devpost, social post |

## 6. Build order and milestones (EST)

| By | Done means |
|---|---|
| 8pm | Repo skeleton. tfclient with record/replay. One live TinyAgent run on a Teknic page with our schema; Verifier confirms at least one quote. CAD: bracket from hard-coded NEMA 23 numbers in the viewer. |
| 11pm | One job end to end on the motor: discover → triage → extract → verify → checks → rank → GLB in viewer, SSE tiles live. Deployed on Vultr. |
| 1:30am | board + tasks on Tiger Data, 2 origin workers, circuit breaker, compliance card, success-by-site panel. |
| 3:30am | case builder, advocates round 1, synthesizer, RFQ draft. Then, if time: cross-exam, critic, gap round. |
| 4am | FEATURE FREEZE. 4-8am: record replay fixtures for the demo, backup video, Devpost text, social post tagging TinyFish. |

Cut order if behind (first cut first): advocates round 2 → critic + gap round → TinyMonitor →
TinyBrowser RFQ form → origin workers (keep motor only) → supplier_1h. Never cut: live agents on
real sites, verifier, code checks, regenerated bracket.

## 7. Tygo's first chunk (hands-on flow applies)

Scaffold inside the existing backend: `backend/app/tfclient/` (record/replay), `backend/app/agents/verifier.py`,
`backend/app/orchestrator/` skeleton with fake workers; apply the `schemas.py` deltas from section 4 first.
Core for Tygo to write (failing tests left by the agent):
- `classify_outcome(run) -> Outcome`: COMPLETED with `status != success`, all-null data,
  "access denied"/CAPTCHA text, or FAILED map to `blocked | not_found | auth_required |
  incomplete | error`; only a clean result is `success`.
- `verify_claim(claim, html_or_pdf_text) -> Claim`: normalize whitespace/commas, find the quote,
  check the number in the quote equals `raw_value`, set `verified` and `verify_method`.
Test cases to include: a COMPLETED run with all nulls; a quote present but number differs
(promo vs regular price); a quote split across tags; "Designed in USA" must not become T1/T2.

## 8. Environment and secrets

- Python 3.12 for anything importing CadQuery (`pip install cadquery` worked, 2.8.0; `cad/` has its own Dockerfile). The Hermes
  sandbox's `/tmp` is a 512 MB tmpfs: create venvs under `/home/pn` there.
- Keys only in a gitignored `.env`: `TINYFISH_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, Tiger connection
  string, Vultr. Never in prompts or goals (AGENTS.md: session transcripts are pushed).
- TinyFish free daily allowance: 12,000 Search, 1,000 Fetch URLs. Agent concurrency per account
  (assume 2 until the booth answers). `max_steps` is beta; use `max_duration_seconds`.
- Pushing: the sandbox token may not push to Kingsolima/HackWestern-2026; Tygo pushes from host.
- Commits: no AI co-author lines (AGENTS.md).

## 9. Still open (ask in person)

- TinyFish booth: concurrency bump for our accounts; `max_steps` beta today?
- Organizers: can one team win more than one MLH prize?
- Demo BOM: must be a covered device and produce an honest before/after domestic %.

## 10. Known-good targets for the demo (pre-identify, verify again in hour one)

- Teknic ClearPath-SD, NEMA 23/34 integrated servo, from $265, "New York manufacturing plant"
  (T2). https://teknic.com/products/clearpath-brushless-dc-servo-motors/clearpath-sd/
- Moog Animatics SmartMotor SM23165D, "produced in our Murphy, NC facility" (model-specific).
  https://animatics.com/news-and-events/moog-animatics-lead-time-improvement
- Pittman NEMA 23 brushless: HQ address only (T3), the verifier's "Review" example.
- Distributors: DigiKey (Cloudflare) and Mouser (Akamai) blocked a plain headless browser; test
  through TinyFish stealth + US proxy before relying on them. Mouser lists Country of Origin per
  SKU when reachable.

## 11. Kickoff prompt for the next session

> Load the `agentic-coding-workflow` and `hackathon-ideation` skills. Read
> `docs/HANDOFF-v3.md`, then `docs/design/07-agent-architecture.md` and `04-architecture.md`.
> Design is approved. `git fetch`, branch from `origin/main` (teammates' scaffold is there; see
> section 4 for the deltas). Start Tygo's first chunk (section 7): scaffold tfclient record/replay,
> verifier and orchestrator skeleton, leave failing tests for `classify_outcome` and
> `verify_claim` for me to write. Python 3.12 venv under /home/pn.

content.text:
The v3 docs are now in your working copy: you're on the `design/v3` branch, and your uncommitted `HANDOFF-v2.md` edits came along untouched. Start with [docs/HANDOFF-v3.md](docs/HANDOFF-v3.md), then open [docs/design/architecture.html](docs/design/architecture.html) in a browser for the diagram.

**How v3 changes the plan**

v3 replaces the next steps I gave you. The main differences:

- **More than one motor search.** An orchestrator runs one worker per BOM line. A swap worker hunts for replacement drive motors, and 2–3 origin workers try to prove where expensive parts like the battery and compute board are made.
- **Cheaper searching.** Workers use the free TinySearch and TinyFetch first, with Gemini reading the pages. TinyAgent and its live tiles only run when a page needs clicking.
- **A shared "blackboard" in Tiger Data.** Only the verifier can write confirmed facts to it, and all workers read from it.
- **Record/replay from the start.** Every TinyFish and Gemini call can be saved and replayed, so the demo works even if live sites fail. The UI shows a LIVE or REPLAY badge.
- **A synthesis step.** Three "advocates" (cost, performance, US-first) argue their case, a writer summarizes, and a Gemini critic can send back one round of follow-up questions. LLMs still never produce numbers or verdicts.
- **A new demo robot:** about 5 kg, direct drive, 60 mm wheels.
- **Real motor targets are already picked:** Teknic ClearPath-SD, Moog SM23165D and Pittman (§10).

**New milestones**

| By | Done means |
|---|---|
| **8pm** | Record/replay client, one live TinyAgent run on the Teknic page, the verifier confirms a quote, and the bracket shows in the viewer (done). |
| 11pm | One full job end to end with live tiles, deployed on Vultr |
| 1:30am | Blackboard on Tiger Data, origin workers, compliance card, success-by-site panel |
| 3:30am | Advocates, synthesis, RFQ draft |
| 4am | Feature freeze |

**Things that affect code we already wrote**

1. **The new robot breaks the current CAD model.** It's built around 70 mm-radius wheels so a NEMA 34 motor clears the plate. If 60 mm wheels means 60 mm diameter, the motor shaft sits only 30 mm off the ground, and even a NEMA 23 hits the floor. Owner 1 and Owner 3 need to settle on the wheel size; the CAD code throws an error if a motor can't fit.
2. **§4 lists the code changes for the first hour.** The motor schema switches to a list of specs with quotes, the checks gain continuous and peak torque and ground clearance, and compliance moves to landed cost (price plus freight and duty). It keeps our module and table names, so it builds on what's already on main.
3. **Tygo writes two functions personally.** §7 says agents scaffold the code and leave failing tests, and Tygo writes `classify_outcome` and `verify_claim`. I won't write those two.
4. **The v3 branch isn't on main yet.** You can read it locally now. Run `git switch main` to go back, or merge `design/v3` into main when the team agrees on it.

Do you want me to start the §7 scaffolding (record/replay client, orchestrator skeleton, verifier with failing tests) on a branch from main?

## 4. Data shapes

```python
class Requirement(BaseModel):          # from the robot spec, owner 3
    mass_kg: float; wheel_radius_m: float; n_drive: int; gear_ratio: float; eta: float
    crr: float; slope_deg: float; accel_mps2: float; v_max_mps: float; v_bus: float
    safety_factor: float; frame_allowed: list[str]; inboard_room_mm: float
    min_ground_clearance_mm: float; wheel_bore_mm: float

class Source(BaseModel):
    url: str; kind: Literal["page", "pdf"]; fetched_at: datetime
    html_key: str | None               # object-storage key of the captured html/pdf
    via: Literal["tinyfetch", "tinyagent", "replay"]

class Claim(BaseModel):                # one fact, never a bare number
    candidate_id: str
    field: str                         # e.g. "continuous_torque", "country_of_origin"
    raw_value: str; raw_unit: str | None; quote: str
    source: Source
    si_value: float | None = None      # filled by units.py, never by an LLM
    extracted_by: Literal["tinyagent", "gemini_text", "gemini_vision"]
    verified: bool = False
    verify_method: Literal["html_quote", "pdf_text", "none"] = "none"

class OriginEvidence(BaseModel):
    country: str | None
    tier: Literal["T1", "T2", "T3", "rejected", "none"]
    claim_id: str | None

class Candidate(BaseModel):
    id: str; manufacturer: str | None; part_number: str | None
    motor_type: Literal["servo_integrated", "bldc", "stepper", "brushed_dc", "unknown"]
    nema_frame: Literal["17", "23", "34", "other"] | None
    claims: list[Claim]; origin: OriginEvidence
    status: Literal["found", "blocked", "not_found", "auth_required", "incomplete"]

class RunRecord(BaseModel):            # one per external call; goes to Tiger Data agent_runs
    run_id: str; job_id: str; product: Literal["search", "fetch", "agent", "browser", "monitor", "gemini"]
    site: str; started_at: datetime; duration_s: float
    tf_status: str | None              # PENDING/RUNNING/COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED
    outcome: Literal["success", "blocked", "not_found", "auth_required", "incomplete", "error"]

content.text:
I checked the design docs, and I need to correct one thing I said earlier. The 60 mm is the wheel **radius**, not the diameter (03-v2-review says "r = 60 mm"), so NEMA 23 does fit. The real CAD problem is NEMA 34.

**Before (main) vs after (v3)**

| Area | Before (what's on main) | After (v3) |
|---|---|---|
| **Demo robot** | 8 kg, belt drive (G = 3), 70 mm wheel radius | ~5 kg, direct drive (G = 1), 60 mm wheel radius |
| **Motor data** | One flat record per motor: `rated_torque_nm`, `voltage_v`, `price_usd`… | Each spec is a separate **Claim** with the value and unit as written, the exact quote and the source URL. A spec only counts once the verifier confirms the quote is on the page. |
| **Motor type** | Not tracked | `servo_integrated`, `bldc`, `stepper` or `brushed_dc`. The rules differ per type, and steppers are capped at Review. |
| **Checks** | 4 checks: torque, speed, exact voltage match, length fit | 7 checks: continuous torque, peak torque, speed, voltage range, envelope fit, **ground clearance** and **shaft-vs-wheel-bore**. Real drop_in/close badge. |
| **Compliance** | Domestic % by unit cost, origin is a plain country code | Domestic % by **landed cost** (price + freight + duty), only origin tiers T1/T2 count as US, must be strictly above 65%, and the COTS note is replaced |
| **Agents** | One `find_candidates()` stub | An orchestrator plus swap and origin workers, record/replay, and the synthesis step |
| **Database** | 3 hypertables, one aggregate, `design_variants` | Adds `board` (the blackboard) and `tasks`, plus new columns on `agent_runs` and `price_observations`, and a `supplier_1h` aggregate |
| **API** | `GET /api/robot`, `/api/compliance`, `POST /api/checks`, `/api/runs` (stub) | `POST /jobs`, `GET /jobs/{id}`, `GET /jobs/{id}/events` (live updates over SSE), `GET /designs/{id}/glb` and `/step` |

**What breaks when you apply v3**

1. **The motor schema change breaks four places.** `checks.py`, the `/api/checks` route, `frontend/src/types.ts` and the backend tests all read flat fields like `motor.rated_torque_nm`. They have to change together in one commit, or the tests and the frontend checks table stop working.
2. **The CAD model rejects NEMA 34.** With a 60 mm wheel radius, the motor shaft sits 44 mm above the plate, but a NEMA 34 needs 48 mm, so `robot()` raises an error instead of building. NEMA 17 and 23 still work. This is v3's known issue ("NEMA 34 leaves about 4 mm"). The fix is to make NEMA 34 fail the new ground-clearance check instead of crashing, or to lower the plate.
3. **The requirement field names conflict.** 04-architecture renames fields (`n_drive_motors` to `n_drive`, `efficiency` to `eta`, `bus_voltage_v` to `v_bus`, `envelope_mm` to `inboard_room_mm`), but HANDOFF-v3 §4 says keep the existing names and only add new ones. Pick one before Owners 2 and 3 both edit `schemas.py`. I'd keep the existing names, since §4 is the newer instruction.
4. **The frontend's API calls go stale.** `api.ts` calls `/api/...`; v3 uses `/jobs` with SSE events. The current panels keep working until the old routes are removed.
5. **The demo numbers change.** `demo_robot.json` needs the new robot and a BOM with real prices, origins, freight and duty, so the 37.9% domestic figure will change.

**What doesn't break**
- **The database schema.** v3 worries the `FILTER` clause might fail, but we already ran it on TimescaleDB today and it worked. v3 adds tables and columns rather than replacing them.
- **Docker, CI, the Makefile and the Entire setup.**
- **The bracket code**, including the NEMA table, which v3 says is better than its own CAD spike.

The safest order is: first agree on the field names (3), then make one commit that changes the schema, checks, tests and frontend types together (1). Do you want me to do that on a branch?

content.text:
No. Nothing is connected to Tiger Data right now.

- **`.env` points at a local database**, not Tiger Cloud. It's probably still the default value copied from `.env.example`, which targets the TimescaleDB container on your own machine.
- **That local container is stopped**, so even that connection is refused.

**How to fix it**

To use the **real Tiger Data cloud** (needed for the sponsor prize and the Vultr deploy):
1. In the Tiger Cloud console, create a service, or open the one your team already made, and copy its connection string. It looks like `postgres://tsdbadmin:…@<id>.tsdb.cloud.timescale.com:<port>/tsdb?sslmode=require`.
2. Paste it into `.env` as `DATABASE_URL=...` yourself. Don't paste it into this chat, because transcripts are pushed to the public repo.
3. Load the tables: `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f db/schema.sql`. Or I can run that step from code without printing the connection string.

To use the **local database for development** (no account needed):
```bash
make db
```
That starts the local TimescaleDB container with the schema already loaded, and your current `.env` will connect to it.

I'd use local for building today and switch to Tiger Cloud before deploying to Vultr. Once you've updated `.env`, tell me and I'll re-run the check and load the schema.

content.text: can you explain simply to a beginner what is left to do?

The app's job is to replace a robot's motor with a US-made one, prove the new motor works, and redraw the robot to fit it. Here's how far along each part is.

**✅ Done**
- **The project skeleton:** folders, settings and tests, so the team can work without stepping on each other.
- **The 3D robot:** it redraws itself when you change the motor size, and you can see it in the browser.
- **The website shell:** the page exists, with empty boxes waiting for real data.
- **The database design:** the tables are written, but nothing is connected yet.

**⬜ Left to do, in order**

1. **Teach the AI shoppers to find motors (the biggest job).** Agents visit real motor websites (Teknic, Moog, Pittman) and copy down the specs, price and where each motor is made. A "recorder" also saves every visit, so the demo can replay it if the live sites fail on stage.
2. **Fact-check what the shoppers bring back.** Code re-opens each page and confirms the exact words are really there, because AI sometimes makes things up. Only checked facts move on.
3. **Do the math.** Plain code, never AI, answers: Is the motor strong enough? Fast enough? Right voltage? Does it fit, including not scraping the floor? And what % of the robot is now US-made, counting shipping and tariffs? Part of this exists, but v3 changed the rules.
4. **Pick the winners.** Choose three designs: cheapest, best performing and most American.
5. **Connect everything to one button.** Click Find and Redesign, and you watch the agents work live, the checks fill in, and the robot redraw.
6. **Write the explanation.** AI writes a short case for each design and an RFQ email to the supplier. It explains, but never makes up numbers.
7. **Put it online.** Connect the real Tiger Data database, run the app on a Vultr server and give it a domain name.
8. **Demo prep:** record a backup video, write the Devpost page and post on social media tagging TinyFish.

**⏰ Deadlines tonight**

| By | Goal |
|---|---|
| 8pm | One agent successfully reads one real motor page, and the fact-checker confirms it |
| 11pm | The button works end to end and the app is online |
| 1:30am | The database is connected and more parts get checked |
| 3:30am | The AI explanations and the RFQ draft work |
| 4am | Stop adding features and only polish the demo |

**The one thing that matters most right now** is step 1: getting an agent to read the Teknic motor page. Everything else depends on it, and it's the step most likely to hit surprises, like websites blocking bots.

      "language": "en",
      "text": "This page is the shortest high-signal context dump for coding agents integrating TinyFish. **Always use the official SDKs** — they handle authentication, SSE streaming, retries, and typed responses so you don’t have to.

For complete API reference in a single file, use llms-full.txt (218KB, includes all code examples). Note that `llms.txt` is just an index — agents should use `llms-full.txt` for full context.

If you’re running inside an MCP-compatible host (Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Command Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, ChatGPT), connect via MCP instead of the REST API. Most hosts sign in with OAuth and need no API key management; Command Code connects with a TinyFish API key.

```

```

See the MCP Integration guide for all supported clients and available tools.

## Install the SDK

```
pip install -U tinyfish
```

```
npm install @tiny-fish/sdk@latest
```

| API | Typical Latency | Suggested Timeout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent (sync) | 15-60s | 120s |
| Agent (SSE) | 15-60s (streaming) | N/A (SSE) |
| Search | 1-3s | 10s |
| Fetch | 1-20s | 150s |
| Browser (create) | 10-30s | 60s |

*Fetch: backend timeout is 110s per URL; requests are also subject to a 120s CDN ceiling. Set client timeout to 150s to receive timeout errors cleanly.*

## Authentication

Set your API key (get one from agent.tinyfish.ai/api-keys):

```
export TINYFISH_API_KEY=REDACTED SDKs read `TINYFISH_API_KEY` from the environment automatically. See Authentication for more details.

## Choose the Right TinyFish API

| API | Use it when | Docs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TinyAgent | You want TinyFish to execute a goal on a real website | TinyAgent reference |
| Research | You want a cited report synthesized from many sources | Research overview |
| Search | You want ranked web results for a query | Search overview |
| Fetch | You want extracted page content from one or more URLs | Fetch overview |
| Browser | You want a remote browser session for direct Playwright/CDP control | Browser overview |

### Quick Decision Tree

* **Need data from a URL?** — TinyAgent (goal-based extraction) or TinyFetch (raw page content)
* **Need search results?** — TinySearch
* **Need browser control?** — TinyBrowser (direct Playwright/CDP access)
* **Need logged-in state across recurring runs?** — Create a TinyProfile, then run with `use_profile: true`

## Authenticated or Recurring Runs

When a task should reuse a login session, use **TinyProfiles** first. Do not make the agent log in from scratch every run unless the task explicitly needs a fresh browser. TinyProfiles are saved browser state for a site or account. They are different from `browser_profile: "lite" | "stealth"`, which only chooses the browser runtime mode.

1

Create and set up a profile

Use the TinyProfiles API to create a profile, start a setup session, connect to `cdp_url` with Playwright/Puppeteer/CDP, sign in, and save with `session_id`. The dashboard setup UI is a manual helper.

2

Run with saved state

Pass `use_profile: true` to use the default profile, or add `profile_id` for a specific profile.

3

Repair stale sessions with Vault

For long-lived workflows, pair profiles with `use_vault: true` so TinyFish can sign in again when cookies expire.

```
result = client.agent.run(
    url="https://app.example.com/dashboard",
    goal="Summarize the account health dashboard.",
    use_profile=True,
    use_vault=True,
)
```

```
const run = await client.agent.run({
  url: "https://app.example.com/dashboard",
  goal: "Summarize the account health dashboard.",
  use_profile: true,
  use_vault: true,
});
```

`use_profile: true` uses the default TinyProfile. Use `profile_id` when the user names a specific TinyProfile; `profile_id` requires `use_profile: true`:

```
result = client.agent.run(
    url="https://app.example.com/dashboard",
    goal="Summarize the latest invoice, including the amount due and payment deadline.",
    use_profile=True,
    profile_id="prof_abc123def4567890",
)
```

```
const run = await client.agent.run({
  url: "https://app.example.com/dashboard",
  goal: "Summarize the latest invoice, including the amount due and payment deadline.",
  use_profile: true,
  profile_id: "prof_abc123def4567890",
});
```

## SDK Examples

```
from tinyfish import TinyFish, CompleteEvent

client = TinyFish()

with client.agent.stream(
    url="https://scrapeme.live/shop",
    goal="Extract the first 2 product names and prices. Return as JSON.",
) as stream:
    for event in stream:
        if isinstance(event, CompleteEvent):
            print(event.result_json)
```

```
import { TinyFish } from "@tiny-fish/sdk";

const client = new TinyFish();

const stream = await client.agent.stream({
  url: "https://scrapeme.live/shop",
  goal: "Extract the first 2 product names and prices. Return as JSON.",
});

for await (const event of stream) {
  if (event.type === "COMPLETE") {
    console.log(event.result);
  }
}
```

### Agent — Synchronous

```
from tinyfish import TinyFish, RunStatus

client = TinyFish()

result = client.agent.run(
    url="https://scrapeme.live/shop",
    goal="Extract the first 2 product names and prices. Return as JSON.",
)
if result.status == RunStatus.COMPLETED:
    print(result.result)
```

```
import { TinyFish, RunStatus } from "@tiny-fish/sdk";

const client = new TinyFish();

const run = await client.agent.run({
  url: "https://scrapeme.live/shop",
  goal: "Extract the first 2 product names and prices. Return as JSON.",
});

if (run.status === RunStatus.COMPLETED) {
  console.log(run.result);
}
```

### Search

```
result = client.search.query("web automation tools", location="US", language="en")
print(result)
```

```
const result = await client.search.query({
  query: "web automation tools",
  location: "US",
  language: "en",
});
console.log(result);
```

Use `recency_minutes` for a freshness window, `after_date` / `before_date` for calendar date filters, and `domain_type` for content category:

* `recency_minutes`: integer `1..5256000`
* `after_date` / `before_date`: `YYYY-MM-DD`
* `domain_type`: `"web"` (default) | `"news"` | `"research_paper"`
* `pub_year_min` / `pub_year_max`: integer `0..9999`, inclusive; only supported for `domain_type=research_paper`
* do not combine `recency_minutes` with date filters
* if both dates are present, `after_date <= before_date`
* if both pub\_year bounds are present, `pub_year_min <= pub_year_max`
* `after_date`, `before_date`, and `recency_minutes` are not supported for `domain_type=research_paper` — use `pub_year_min` / `pub_year_max` instead

### Fetch

```
result = client.fetch.get_contents(urls=["https://www.tinyfish.ai/"])
print(result)
```

```
const result = await client.fetch.getContents({
  urls: ["https://www.tinyfish.ai/"],
});
console.log(result);
```

Omit `ttl` for the default cache behavior. Add `ttl` only when freshness matters: set it to `0` when you want a live fetch, or to a positive number of seconds to accept cached entries younger than that window.

### Anti-Detection Mode

For sites with bot protection, add stealth mode and a proxy:

```
from tinyfish import TinyFish, BrowserProfile, ProxyConfig, ProxyCountryCode

client = TinyFish()

result = client.agent.run(
    url="https://protected-site.com",
    goal="Extract pricing data. Return as JSON.",
    browser_profile=BrowserProfile.STEALTH,
    proxy_config=ProxyConfig(enabled=True, country_code=ProxyCountryCode.US),
)
```

```
import { TinyFish, BrowserProfile, ProxyCountryCode } from "@tiny-fish/sdk";

const client = new TinyFish();

const run = await client.agent.run({
  url: "https://protected-site.com",
  goal: "Extract pricing data. Return as JSON.",
  browser_profile: BrowserProfile.STEALTH,
  proxy_config: {
    enabled: true,
    country_code: ProxyCountryCode.US,
  },
});
```

## Expected Latency

| API | Typical Latency | Suggested Timeout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent (sync) | 15-60s | 120s |
| Agent (SSE) | 15-60s (streaming) | N/A (SSE) |
| Search | 1-3s | 10s |
| Fetch | 1-20s | 150s |
| Browser (create) | 10-30s | 60s |

## Prompting

Goal quality determines success rate. Vague goals like “get the data” fail; crafted goals with explicit fields, output format, and edge-case handling succeed consistently.

See the full Prompting Guide for tested patterns, templates, and examples.

## Common Gotchas

1. **TinyBrowser session creation takes 10-30s** — set `timeout=60` on your HTTP client.
2. **TypeScript needs `"type": "module"`** in `package.json` for top-level `await`, or wrap code in `async function main() { ... }; main()`.
3. **`COMPLETED` status does not mean the goal succeeded** — always check `result_json` for failure signals like “captcha”, “blocked”, or “access denied”.
4. **TinyFetch has a 110s per-URL backend timeout** — requests are also subject to a 120s CDN ceiling for the full batch. Set your client timeout to at least 150s.

Raw API Endpoints (cURL)

If you can’t use the SDKs, here are the raw endpoints. All use the `X-API-Key` header for authentication.

### Agent

```
curl -N -X POST https://agent.tinyfish.ai/v1/automation/run-sse \
  -H "X-API-Key: $TINYFISH_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://scrapeme.live/shop",
    "goal": "Extract the first 2 product names and prices. Return JSON."
  }'
```

### Search

```
curl "https://api.search.tinyfish.ai?query=web+automation+tools&location=US&language=en" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $TINYFISH_API_KEY"
```

### Fetch

```
curl -X POST https://api.fetch.tinyfish.ai \
  -H "X-API-Key: $TINYFISH_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"urls": ["https://www.tinyfish.ai/"]}'
```

### Browser

```
curl -X POST https://api.browser.tinyfish.ai \
  -H "X-API-Key: $TINYFISH_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://www.tinyfish.ai"}'
```

## Common Request Body

The three single-run endpoints — `run`, `run-async`, and `run-sse` — accept this JSON body directly. `run-batch` wraps an array of these bodies under `runs`, except `profile_id` and `output_schema`, which are top-level only on the batch request; see Create a Batch of Agent Runs.

```

  "url": "https://example.com",
  "goal": "Find the pricing page and extract all plan details",
  "output_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "title": { "type": "string" },
      "price": { "type": "number" }
    },
    "required": ["title", "price"]
  },
  "browser_profile": "lite",
  "proxy_config": {
    "enabled": true,
    "type": "tinyfish",
    "country_code": "US"
  },
  "agent_config": {
    "mode": "strict",
    "max_steps": 50,
    "max_duration_seconds": 300
  },
  "webhook_url": "https://example.com/webhooks/tinyfish",
  "use_profile": true,
  "profile_id": "prof_abc123def4567890",
  "use_vault": true,
  "credential_item_ids": ["cred:a1b2c3d4:Work:item-xyz"]
}
```

## Stream an Agent Run via SSE

`POST /v1/automation/run-sse`
Streams a live event feed while the automation runs. The protocol itself is documented here since
it isn’t captured by a request/response schema.


| Event type | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `STARTED` | `type`, `run_id`, `timestamp` |
| `STREAMING_URL` | `type`, `run_id`, `streaming_url`, `timestamp` |
| `PROGRESS` | `type`, `run_id`, `purpose`, `timestamp` |
| `HEARTBEAT` | `type`, `timestamp` |
| `COMPLETE` | `type`, `run_id`, `status`, `result?`, `error?`, `timestamp` (on failure, `error` carries `help_url` / `help_message`) |

Example stream:

```
data: {"type":"STARTED","run_id":"run_123","timestamp":"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}

data: {"type":"STREAMING_URL","run_id":"run_123","streaming_url":"https://...","timestamp":"..."}

data: {"type":"PROGRESS","run_id":"run_123","purpose":"Clicking submit button","timestamp":"..."}

data: {"type":"HEARTBEAT","timestamp":"..."}

data: {"type":"COMPLETE","run_id":"run_123","status":"COMPLETED","result":{...},"timestamp":"..."}
```

**Heartbeats:** `HEARTBEAT` events carry no `run_id` and arrive periodically to keep the connection alive during longer gaps between `PROGRESS` events. Ignore any event `type` your client doesn’t explicitly handle.

**Reconnection:** SSE streams do not support `Last-Event-ID` reconnection. If your client disconnects mid-stream, recover by polling `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` until the run reaches a terminal status (`COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, or `CANCELLED`).

## Cache Freshness

By default, Fetch may serve an existing cached entry for the URL when one is available. Pass `ttl` to set a freshness preference in seconds.

```
{
  "urls": ["https://example.com"],
  "ttl": 3600
}
```

* Omit `ttl` to accept any cached entry.
* Set `ttl` to `0` when you want a live fetch.
* Set `ttl` to a positive integer to accept cached entries younger than that many seconds.

---

## Conditional Requests

Skip reprocessing pages that haven’t changed since your last fetch. Set `include_etag_and_last_modified: true` to get `etag` / `last_modified` validators back on each result, save them, then replay the `etag` as `if_none_match` (or the `last_modified` as `if_modified_since`) the next time you fetch that URL.

```
{
  "urls": ["https://example.com"],
  "if_none_match": "W/\"abc123\"",
  "include_etag_and_last_modified": true
}
```

* `if_none_match` and `if_modified_since` are single-URL only — combining either with a batch of URLs returns a `400`.
* When the origin confirms nothing changed, the result comes back with `not_modified: true` so you can skip re-processing.
* Fetch persists nothing — you own storing and replaying the validators.

See the full reference and a worked example.


---

## CSS Selector Scoping

Extract only the part of the page you care about. Pass `include_selectors` (an array of CSS selectors, max 20) to scope extracted content to elements matching any entry, and/or `exclude_selectors` to strip matching elements before extraction.

```
{
  "urls": ["https://example.com/blog/post"],
  "include_selectors": ["article"],
  "exclude_selectors": [".comments", ".newsletter-signup"]
}
```

* Selected content is returned verbatim in your requested format — automatic boilerplate removal is bypassed. Page-level metadata (`title`, `description`, etc.) still comes from the full document.
* `exclude_selectors` is applied first, then `include_selectors` scopes what remains.
* If some entries match and others don’t, the URL still succeeds and the misses are listed in the result’s `unmatched_selectors`. If no entry matches anything, that URL fails with `selector_not_matched` in `errors[]`, carrying `unmatched_selectors` plus `candidate_selectors` retry hints — agents can retry with `include_selectors` drawn from that list. `exclude_selectors` entries that match nothing are a no-op.

See the full reference and a worked example.


---

## Highlights

Add a `highlights` object to a normal Fetch request and, for each URL, get back the passages from that page that best answer your question — ranked, and quoted word-for-word from the page. Highlights are extracted, never generated: every passage is an exact substring of the fetched page, so they can’t paraphrase or hallucinate. When the page doesn’t answer the question, you get an explicit empty list instead of a forced guess.

**Beta:** Highlights is in beta and is enabled per-account — join our Beta program to enable it for your account. Requests that include `highlights` from an account that isn’t enabled return `403 FORBIDDEN`; requests without the field are unaffected.

```
{
  "urls": ["https://example.com/"],
  "format": "markdown",
  "highlights": {
    "query": "what does this company do and who are its main customers",
    "max_snippets": 5
  }
}
```

* `highlights` requires `format: "markdown"`.
* Each result gains a `highlights` array of ranked verbatim passages, best first. An **empty list** means the page was fetched and analyzed and does not answer the query — a deliberate, calibrated signal, not a failure. A **missing field** means highlights could not be computed for that URL (rare and transient — the fetch itself still succeeded, and a retry is safe).
* Include the entity or topic in the query (e.g. “who founded Acme Corp”, not “who founded this company”) — retrieval works on vocabulary overlap with the page, and keyword-poor queries return empty results far more often.
* Typical single-URL highlights request on a live page render: ~1.5–2s; JavaScript-heavy sites can take 10–20s to render server-side. Multi-URL requests process in parallel, so request latency ≈ the slowest URL in the batch.

See the full reference and a worked example.

## Supported Content Types

The TinyFetch handles more than just HTML. See the full content types table in the reference — in short: PDF text extraction works, JSON endpoints return raw JSON, but binary files (images, video) return an error.


---

## Fetch Intent

The optional `purpose` parameter lets you state *why* you are fetching — the underlying goal or task the content will be used for. A URL alone says nothing about what you need from the page. Passing `purpose` gives us additional signal to further inform and deliver better-quality results. It works the same way as the `purpose` parameter in TinySearch.

* `purpose` is always optional. Omitting it leaves fetch behaviour unchanged.
* Keep it to a short phrase or sentence (maximum 2000 characters), for example `Compare pricing tiers across vendors for a procurement report`.

### Quick Decision Tree

## Authenticated or Recurring Runs

When a task should reuse a login session, use **TinyProfiles** first. Do not make the agent log in from scratch every run unless the task explicitly needs a fresh browser. TinyProfiles are saved browser state for a site or account. They are different from `browser_profile: "lite" | "stealth"`, which only chooses the browser runtime mode.

3

## Common Gotchas

1. **TinyBrowser session creation takes 10-30s** — set `timeout=60` on your HTTP client.
2. **TypeScript needs `"type": "module"`** in `package.json` for top-level `await`, or wrap code in `async function main() { ... }; main()`.
3. **`COMPLETED` status does not mean the goal succeeded** — always check `result_json` for failure signals like “captcha”, “blocked”, or “access denied”.
4. **TinyFetch has a 110s per-URL backend timeout** — requests are also subject to a 120s CDN ceiling for the full batch. Set your client timeout to at least 150s.

## Stream an Agent Run via SSE

`POST /v1/automation/run-sse`
Streams a live event feed while the automation runs. The protocol itself is documented here since
it isn’t captured by a request/response schema.


| Event type | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `STARTED` | `type`, `run_id`, `timestamp` |
| `STREAMING_URL` | `type`, `run_id`, `streaming_url`, `timestamp` |
| `PROGRESS` | `type`, `run_id`, `purpose`, `timestamp` |
| `HEARTBEAT` | `type`, `timestamp` |
| `COMPLETE` | `type`, `run_id`, `status`, `result?`, `error?`, `timestamp` (on failure, `error` carries `help_url` / `help_message`) |

Example stream:

```
data: {"type":"STARTED","run_id":"run_123","timestamp":"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}

data: {"type":"STREAMING_URL","run_id":"run_123","streaming_url":"https://...","timestamp":"..."}

data: {"type":"PROGRESS","run_id":"run_123","purpose":"Clicking submit button","timestamp":"..."}

data: {"type":"HEARTBEAT","timestamp":"..."}

data: {"type":"COMPLETE","run_id":"run_123","status":"COMPLETED","result":{...},"timestamp":"..."}
```

**Heartbeats:** `HEARTBEAT` events carry no `run_id` and arrive periodically to keep the connection alive during longer gaps between `PROGRESS` events. Ignore any event `type` your client doesn’t explicitly handle.

**Reconnection:** SSE streams do not support `Last-Event-ID` reconnection. If your client disconnects mid-stream, recover by polling `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` until the run reaches a terminal status (`COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, or `CANCELLED`).

## When to Use Fetch vs the Other APIs

* Use **Fetch** when you already know the URL and need clean extracted page content.

## Fetching Multiple URLs

Submit up to 10 URLs in a single request. Each URL is processed independently — one failure doesn’t affect the others.

```
from tinyfish import TinyFish

client = TinyFish()
result = client.fetch.get_contents(
    urls=[
        "https://www.tinyfish.ai/",
        "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_scraping",
        "https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/index.html",
    ]
)

for page in result.results:
    print(page.url, "→", page.title)

for error in result.errors:
    print("Failed:", error.url, "–", error.error)
```

## Cache Freshness

By default, Fetch may serve an existing cached entry for the URL when one is available. Pass `ttl` to set a freshness preference in seconds.

```
{
  "urls": ["https://example.com"],
  "ttl": 3600
}
```

* Omit `ttl` to accept any cached entry.
* Set `ttl` to `0` when you want a live fetch.
* Set `ttl` to a positive integer to accept cached entries younger than that many seconds.

## Conditional Requests

Skip reprocessing pages that haven’t changed since your last fetch. Set `include_etag_and_last_modified: true` to get `etag` / `last_modified` validators back on each result, save them, then replay the `etag` as `if_none_match` (or the `last_modified` as `if_modified_since`) the next time you fetch that URL.

```
{
  "urls": ["https://example.com"],
  "if_none_match": "W/\"abc123\"",
  "include_etag_and_last_modified": true
}
```

* `if_none_match` and `if_modified_since` are single-URL only — combining either with a batch of URLs returns a `400`.
* When the origin confirms nothing changed, the result comes back with `not_modified: true` so you can skip re-processing.
* Fetch persists nothing — you own storing and replaying the validators.

See the full reference and a worked example.

## CSS Selector Scoping

Extract only the part of the page you care about. Pass `include_selectors` (an array of CSS selectors, max 20) to scope extracted content to elements matching any entry, and/or `exclude_selectors` to strip matching elements before extraction.

```
{
  "urls": ["https://example.com/blog/post"],
  "include_selectors": ["article"],
  "exclude_selectors": [".comments", ".newsletter-signup"]
}
```

* Selected content is returned verbatim in your requested format — automatic boilerplate removal is bypassed. Page-level metadata (`title`, `description`, etc.) still comes from the full document.
* `exclude_selectors` is applied first, then `include_selectors` scopes what remains.
* If some entries match and others don’t, the URL still succeeds and the misses are listed in the result’s `unmatched_selectors`. If no entry matches anything, that URL fails with `selector_not_matched` in `errors[]`, carrying `unmatched_selectors` plus `candidate_selectors` retry hints — agents can retry with `include_selectors` drawn from that list. `exclude_selectors` entries that match nothing are a no-op.

See the full reference and a worked example.


---

## Highlights

Add a `highlights` object to a normal Fetch request and, for each URL, get back the passages from that page that best answer your question — ranked, and quoted word-for-word from the page. Highlights are extracted, never generated: every passage is an exact substring of the fetched page, so they can’t paraphrase or hallucinate. When the page doesn’t answer the question, you get an explicit empty list instead of a forced guess.

**Beta:** Highlights is in beta and is enabled per-account — join our Beta program to enable it for your account. Requests that include `highlights` from an account that isn’t enabled return `403 FORBIDDEN`; requests without the field are unaffected.

```
{
  "urls": ["https://example.com/"],
  "format": "markdown",
  "highlights": {
    "query": "what does this company do and who are its main customers",
    "max_snippets": 5
  }
}
```

* `highlights` requires `format: "markdown"`.
* Each result gains a `highlights` array of ranked verbatim passages, best first. An **empty list** means the page was fetched and analyzed and does not answer the query — a deliberate, calibrated signal, not a failure. A **missing field** means highlights could not be computed for that URL (rare and transient — the fetch itself still succeeded, and a retry is safe).
* Include the entity or topic in the query (e.g. “who founded Acme Corp”, not “who founded this company”) — retrieval works on vocabulary overlap with the page, and keyword-poor queries return empty results far more often.
* Typical single-URL highlights request on a live page render: ~1.5–2s; JavaScript-heavy sites can take 10–20s to render server-side. Multi-URL requests process in parallel, so request latency ≈ the slowest URL in the batch.

See the full reference and a worked example.

## Supported Content Types

The TinyFetch handles more than just HTML. See the full content types table in the reference — in short: PDF text extraction works, JSON endpoints return raw JSON, but binary files (images, video) return an error.

## Fetch Intent

The optional `purpose` parameter lets you state *why* you are fetching — the underlying goal or task the content will be used for. A URL alone says nothing about what you need from the page. Passing `purpose` gives us additional signal to further inform and deliver better-quality results. It works the same way as the `purpose` parameter in TinySearch.

* `purpose` is always optional. Omitting it leaves fetch behaviour unchanged.
* Keep it to a short phrase or sentence (maximum 2000 characters), for example `Compare pricing tiers across vendors for a procurement report`.

# Plan: Step 1, the first live TinyFish agent run on the Teknic ClearPath-SD page

## Context
HANDOFF-v3 §6, 8pm milestone: "tfclient with record/replay. One live TinyAgent run on a Teknic page with our schema; Verifier confirms at least one quote." This step builds the record/replay client and gets one real TinyAgent extraction from Teknic. Every later stage (verify → checks → CAD) depends on that data. The verifier logic belongs to Tygo (v3 §7), so I'll only leave **failing tests** for `classify_outcome` / `verify_claim` (your choice).

What I found:
- **TinyFish API** (docs.tinyfish.ai, checked today): `POST https://agent.tinyfish.ai/v1/automation/run-sse` with the `X-API-Key` header. The body is `{url, goal, output_schema, browser_profile, proxy_config, agent_config:{max_duration_seconds}}`. SSE events: `STARTED`, `STREAMING_URL`, `PROGRESS`, `HEARTBEAT`, `COMPLETE{status,result,error}`. Fetch is `POST https://api.fetch.tinyfish.ai` with `{urls[≤10], format, ttl}` → `{results[], errors[]}`. `max_steps` is beta and returns 403, so I won't send it. A COMPLETED status does not mean the goal succeeded.
- **The Teknic family page** (`…/clearpath-sd/` redirects to `…/clearpath-sd-stepper-replacement/`) has no per-model specs. Torque, speed, voltage, price and length are on model pages reached through `…/all-clearpath-models/` (a JS table). The US manufacturing claim is on another page (e.g. `/about/`). So this is a true multi-page "needs_interaction" job.
- **The contract**: `docs/design/schemas/motor_candidate.tinyfish.json` and the checker `spikes/check_tf_schema.py`. Both exist only on `origin/design/v3`, not on main yet.

## Branch
`swap-finder-swarm` (Trail #3). First `git merge origin/main`, then `git merge origin/design/v3` so the v3 schema, docs and spike are present. Your local uncommitted `docs/HANDOFF-v2.md` edits stay uncommitted and untouched.

## Files (all under `backend/` unless noted)
1. `app/config.py`: add `tf_mode: str = "replay"` (`live` | `replay`) and `fixtures_dir = REPO_ROOT/"data/fixtures"`. Add `TF_MODE=replay` to `.env.example`.
2. `app/tfclient/recorder.py`: fixture key = sha256 of `(product, canonical JSON request body)`. The API key is never part of the body or the fixture. `save(key, record)` and `load(key)` read and write `data/fixtures/tinyfish/<product>-<key[:16]>.json` = `{product, request, events|response, recorded_at}`.
3. `app/tfclient/client.py`: `TinyFishClient(mode)` using `httpx.AsyncClient`:
   - `async agent_run_sse(url, goal, output_schema, max_duration_seconds=240, browser_profile="lite")` is an async iterator of event dicts. In live mode it streams, yields each event with `live=True`, and saves the full event list when the stream ends. In replay mode it yields the recorded events with `live=False`. A missing fixture raises `FixtureMissing`.
   - `async fetch(urls, format="markdown", ttl=None)`: same live/replay pattern.
   - Errors and logs never include headers.
4. `app/agents/motor_schema.py`: loads `docs/design/schemas/motor_candidate.tinyfish.json`, plus a Pydantic `TfMotorCandidate` and `TfSpec` mirroring it, used to validate the agent's `result`.
5. `app/agents/teknic.py`: `TEKNIC_URL` and `build_goal()`. The goal tells the agent to open the ClearPath-SD model list, pick **one NEMA 23 SDSK** model, open its spec page, and fill `specs[]` (continuous/peak torque, max speed, supply voltage min/max, body length, shaft diameter, price) with the value and unit as written, an **exact quote** and `source_url`. It also finds Teknic's statement of where ClearPath is manufactured → `origin_quote` / `origin_source_url`. Null when not found, `status=blocked` on a CAPTCHA, never guess.
6. `scripts/teknic_probe.py` (run as `uv run python scripts/teknic_probe.py [--live]`): runs the agent through the client, prints `STREAMING_URL` (open it to watch live) and progress lines, validates the `COMPLETE` result against `TfMotorCandidate`, and prints a spec table and the origin quote. In live mode it records the fixture so replay reproduces it offline.
7. `tests/test_tfclient.py` (passing): replay yields the recorded events with `live=False`; a missing fixture raises; the fixture key doesn't change with dict key order; the v3 schema passes `spikes/check_tf_schema.py`.
8. `tests/test_verifier_todo.py` (**failing on purpose**, marked so CI still passes). Stubs `classify_outcome(run)` / `verify_claim(claim, text)` in `app/agents/verifier.py` that raise `NotImplementedError`. The tests cover v3 §7's cases: a COMPLETED run with all nulls → not success; a quote present but the number differs (promo vs regular price); a quote split across tags; "Designed in USA" ≠ T1/T2. Use `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="Tygo implements")` so they show as expected-fail and flip to errors once they pass.
9. `data/fixtures/tinyfish/`: commit the recorded Teknic fixture. It's public page content only, so it's safe in a public repo. The demo replays from it.

Not in scope: Gemini, the orchestrator, `schemas.py` v3 deltas, the frontend. (Those come next.)

## Cost and safety
- **One** live TinyAgent run with `max_duration_seconds=240`, run once by me after you confirm, and no retry loop. If it errors, I check run status before running anything again (v3 §5). Fetch calls are free.
- The key is read from `.env` by the app only and is never printed. The fixture stores the request body without headers.

## Verification
1. `make test`: new tests pass, the verifier tests show `xfail`, ruff is clean.
2. `uv run python scripts/teknic_probe.py --live`: prints a streaming URL, progress, a validated result with ≥1 spec and quotes, and saves a fixture.
3. `uv run python scripts/teknic_probe.py` (replay): identical output with no network.
4. A manual sanity check: confirm one returned quote appears on its `source_url`, using a free TinyFetch.
5. Commit to `swap-finder-swarm` (no AI co-author lines), `entire trail ready`, push. Merging is your call.

A live run costs TinyFish agent credit. Open the printed streaming URL to watch it.

import argparse

from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

async def main(live: bool, max_duration: int) -> int:
    client = TinyFishClient("live" if live else "replay")
    print(f"mode: {client.mode} | url: {TEKNIC_URL}")

        TEKNIC_URL, build_goal(), output_schema(), max_duration_seconds=max_duration

"""Known-good demo target: Teknic ClearPath-SD (HANDOFF-v3 §10).

The family page has no per-model specs; they sit on model pages behind the model list, and
the manufacturing claim is on another page. That makes it a real multi-page TinyAgent job.
"""

TEKNIC_URL = "https://teknic.com/products/clearpath-brushless-dc-servo-motors/clearpath-sd/"


def build_goal() -> str:
    return """\
You are a sourcing engineer collecting verifiable specs for ONE motor. Do not buy, log in, \
fill forms or sign up for anything.

1. On this Teknic ClearPath-SD page, go to the list of ClearPath-SD models \
("All ClearPath models", filtered to SDSK if possible).
2. Pick ONE NEMA 23 SDSK model (part number starts with CPM-SDSK-23) and open its \
specification / model information page.
3. From that model's page, fill `specs` with every one of these that is shown: \
continuous_torque, peak_torque, max_speed, supply_voltage_min, supply_voltage_max, \
body_length, shaft_diameter, price. For each spec:
   - value = the number exactly as shown, unit = the unit exactly as shown (e.g. "oz-in", \
"N-m", "RPM", "VDC", "in", "mm", "USD"); do not convert units.
   - quote = the exact text copied from the page that contains that number (a short \
label + value), character for character.
   - source_url = the URL of the page where you read it.
   - at_speed_value / at_speed_unit only if the page ties the torque to a speed, else null.
4. Find where Teknic states ClearPath motors are manufactured (try the model page, then the \
About page). Put the exact sentence in origin_quote, its page URL in origin_source_url, and \
the country it names in country_of_origin. "Designed in" or a headquarters address is NOT \
a manufacturing statement: leave origin fields null in that case.
5. manufacturer = "Teknic", part_number = the model's part number, motor_type = \
"servo_integrated", nema_frame = "23", product_url = the model page URL, datasheet_url = a \
manual/datasheet PDF link if one is on the model page, else null.

Rules: never guess or fill placeholders; use null (or omit a spec) when not shown. \
If a CAPTCHA, bot check or access-denied page blocks you, return status "blocked" with the \
reason. If you cannot find any NEMA 23 SDSK model, return status "not_found". If some fields \
are missing, return status "incomplete" and list what is missing in reason. Otherwise status \
"success".
"""
